USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Acid protection of the formulation

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient with difficulty swallowing opens a delayed-release omeprazole capsule, crushes the enteric-coated granules and mixes the powder into food. The pharmacist explains why the granules must remain intact. Which formulation purpose is most directly undermined by crushing them?

  1. Maintenance of a gastric ulcer coating
  2. Direct stimulation of esophageal peristalsis
  3. Protection of acid-labile drug until intestinal delivery
  4. Prevention of all hepatic metabolism
  5. Conversion of the drug into an antacid
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Protection of acid-labile drug until intestinal delivery

Enteric protection limits degradation of acid-labile omeprazole in the stomach; administration instructions should preserve the granules.

Understanding the options

Protection of acid-labile drug until intestinal delivery
Enteric protection limits degradation of acid-labile omeprazole in the stomach; administration instructions should preserve the granules.
Prevention of all hepatic metabolism
Enteric coating does not eliminate hepatic metabolism.
Conversion of the drug into an antacid
Crushing does not turn a PPI into a neutralizing salt.
Maintenance of a gastric ulcer coating
The granules are not a sucralfate-like ulcer barrier.
Direct stimulation of esophageal peristalsis
Peristalsis is not the formulation's purpose.
